transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Ben (Redwood SE), Marcus (CTO), Priya (ML Lead), Elena (DevOps)

[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda - ben will do a walk through of the model catalog, show compatibility matrices and benchmark samples, then we can talk security and next steps.
[00:18] Marcus: yea thanks, we just want to see how you pick open models, how you profile latency and cost, and whether dedicated nodes make sense for our synchronous triage flows.
[00:28] Ben: great, jumping in - opening the Redwood Console, model catalog section. top left you can filter by task - generation, chat, embeddings - and by architecture. we surface open models like Mistral, Llama-3, Falcon, and some community weights. each entry has a Redwood-verified performance profile: measured p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, memory footprint, and recommended quantization.
[01:05] Priya: quick question - are those benchmarks run on hosted infra or your dedicated pools? numbers can vary by kernel optimizations.
[01:12] Ben: good point. our catalog shows both hosted (multi-tenant) numbers and a dedicated profile run on a representative GPU shape. we annotate hardware used (A100, H100, RTX-like) and quantization level, like 8-bit or 4-bit. we show expected degradation when more aggressive quantization is used.
[01:40] Elena: is the hardware column always present? we run k8s on-prem so we need a compatibility matrix to decide quantization and kernel selection.
[01:47] Ben: yes - compatibility matrix shows model to supported quantizations (fp16, int8, 4-bit), supported sequence lengths, and kernel availability per runtime (our serving runtime vs open-source backends). note: kv cache for long chat context speedups.
[02:12] Marcus: can you show an example comparing Llama-3 vs Mistral in p95 latency for a 1k token response?
[02:19] Ben: sure, pulling up the benchmark sheet. Mistral 7B on H100 4-bit, p50 is about 120ms per token, p95 around 280ms for a 1k end-to-end in our tests. Llama-3 13B is slower, p95 closer to 420ms on same hardware but sometimes better quality. we also show cost-per-token extrapolated at hosted rates and estimated on Dedicated based on footprint and batching.
[03:05] Priya: ok that's helpful. can you explain how batching affects observed latency? our workload is mostly synchronous - 200 qps peaks with 50 concurrent users - so batching is tricky.
[03:19] Ben: absolutely. in the Optimize tab we have recommended batching and prefix caching settings per workload profile. for synchronous low-latency paths we recommend small batch sizes and aggressive KV cache warmers; for high throughput async jobs we suggest batch windows and larger batch sizes. Optimize will auto-suggest config based on sample token distributions.
[03:45] Aisha: also, for Dedicated you can reserve a sized pool so you don't get noisy-neighbor variability, and we offer burst capacity options.
[03:55] Elena: about network - if we go Private (VPC), what's the setup for peering? we have strict firewall rules.
[04:02] Ben: for Private we offer VPC peering or private link and customer-managed subnets. you can bring-your-own KMS to keep keys in your HSM. audit logs are streamed to your SIEM. we've done health customers with similar constraints.
[04:20] Marcus: security is big - SOC2 plus encryption at rest and in transit, SSO/SAML integration for console?
[04:26] Aisha: yes SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC at route/token level, and detailed audit logs. we'll share our security pack after the call.
[04:37] Priya: back to model catalog - is there an easy way to compare across models with our own prompts? we want to pick 2-3 candidates for POC.
[04:46] Ben: you can upload a prompt set to the Benchmark tab and run against selected models. we produce a matrix with latency, cost, and quality heuristics like perplexity and pass rates. quality heuristics can be tailored, for example hallucination rate metrics for clinical text.
[05:10] Marcus: can we run that on a Dedicated pool so numbers match production?
[05:15] Ben: yes, we can provision a short-lived dedicated run for benchmarking; we'll need your prompts and expected concurrency to tune batch windows.
[05:30] Priya: what about quantization? some of our models are sensitive to 4-bit - do you recommend 4-bit for Llama-3?
[05:37] Ben: depends. 4-bit often saves 2-4x memory and reduces cost, but quality delta varies by model. in the catalog we flag models that are 4-bit friendly and ones where 8-bit or fp16 is recommended. we publish a small quality delta table.
[05:57] Elena: who owns runtime upgrades? if patching kernels or switching to a new attention kernel, how are rollouts handled?
[06:04] Ben: rollout is controlled. Dedicated customers get opt-in windows, Private can control control-plane updates. for hosted, we do canary rollouts and notify customers; if there's a regression we can pin to older kernels.
[06:22] Marcus: timeline - we want a pilot in Jan. any blockers?
[06:28] Aisha: timeline looks doable. first we run benchmarks this month, then POC scoping and contract for Dedicated capacity in early Jan.
[06:35] Priya: question on data residency - some PHI can't leave region. do you offer region isolation?
[06:41] Ben: yes, we have region-specific hosted endpoints and Private installs; for strict residency you'd likely move to Private or Dedicated in region with enforced egress controls.
[07:00] Ben: demoing the compatibility matrix UI - select a model and it highlights supported runtimes, max context, recommended batch sizes, and known inference quirks like layernorm f32 fallback.
[07:25] Priya: I see a column for tokenization mismatch - we've hit that before with clinical tokenization causing off-by-one in truncation.
[07:31] Ben: we show tokenizer used and offer custom tokenizers on Private, and provide pre and post-tokenization hooks via the API.
[07:48] Marcus: any partners for on-prem packaging? our infra team prefers a tested appliance.
[07:54] Aisha: we work with OEM partners for on-prem reference architecture; we can loop in partnerships team if you want an appliance-style delivery.
[08:05] Elena: can you show the API call flow for model selection and fallback? we need automatic fallback to cheaper model on overload.
[08:12] Ben: the API accepts a model routing policy: primary model, fallback candidate, latency SLO threshold, and cost tier. if primary exceeds p95 threshold or capacity, it routes to fallback. we also have automatic rollbacks for detected regression.
[08:35] Marcus: do you support function or tool calling? our triage needs tool invocations for knowledge lookups.
[08:40] Ben: yes, we support structured tool calling and streaming in both hosted and Dedicated runtimes.
[08:47] Priya: regarding evals for hallucination on clinical notes - do you have built-in tooling?
[08:52] Ben: we have an Evals integration that runs test sets and summarizes regression alerts and quality trendlines in Console. you can attach prompt sets and golden references.
[09:10] Aisha: recapping the ask - Sunguard wants low-latency sync workflows with PHI controls. agreed to run benchmark with your prompt set on Dedicated configuration and come back with a cost, latency, and quality matrix.
[09:25] Marcus: sounds good. any immediate blockers on our side?
[09:28] Priya: just packaging the prompt set and confirming firewall rules.
[09:31] Elena: I'll scope firewall and VPC info - might need a network stub for peering.
[09:37] Ben: ok we'll send a list of required ports and sample peering config.
[09:45] Ben: example benchmark output - matrix comparing Mistral-7B at 4-bit, Llama-3-13B at 8-bit, and a small RWX-2 variant. columns: p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, memory footprint, cost per 1k tokens, recommended batch size.
[10:12] Priya: the cost per 1k tokens looks optimistic versus our numbers - is that pre or post caching?
[10:17] Ben: those are raw per-token inference costs; we also show adjusted costs with prefix caching enabled. caching can reduce cost for repeat prompts by up to 60 percent in chatty workflows.
[10:30] Marcus: one final security question - can we bring our own KMS and rotate keys on every deploy?
[10:36] Aisha: yes BYOK is supported; rotation policies can be customer-driven via your KMS. we can also show audit logs for key usage.
[10:46] Elena: how do you handle data retention for prompts and responses? we need TTL and opt-out.
[10:50] Ben: retention is configurable per account; for Private you can disable retention entirely. hosted has retention policies and you can opt out of logging request and response payloads.
[11:05] Marcus: good. next steps?
[11:09] Aisha: we'll email the security pack and pricing; Ben will request the sample prompt set and provision a dedicated benchmark run. propose POC scoping week of Dec 20th.
[11:17] Priya: will share prompt set and expected QPS by Tuesday.
[11:20] Elena: I'll send a network requirements doc to your team.
[11:25] Ben: thanks all, we'll follow up with the benchmark link and results.
[11:30] Marcus: thanks, helpful session.
[11:34] Aisha: thanks everyone - end call.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard tokens and minor speaker overlaps. natural pauses and fillers present.
